newsitem.title: UK: UK says budget date not decided, June 10 possible.
newsitem.headline: UK says budget date not decided, June 10 possible.

text.p: Britain's new Labour government may hold a mini-budget on June 10, a month earlier than most analysts expect, but no date has yet been set, a spokesman for Britain's Treasury said.

Asked about a report in Saturday's Sun newspaper which said Prime Minister Tony Blair and Chancellor of the Exchequer (finance minister) Gordon Brown planned a June 10 budget to maintain the pace of their reforms, the spokesman said: "The date genuinely hasn't been decided yet. June 10 is a possible date."

Labour has long said it would present an emergency budget soon after an election victory to implement its proposed windfall tax on the profits of privatised utilities, but July has generally seen as the most likely date for such a move.
